scene: On the sloop's deck at dawn, the Navigator (tall, thin man of about thirty-five, curly black hair to his shoulders, thin mustache, long gray coat) stands at the center holding a wooden backstaff in one mitten hand and a large unrolled chart in the other, sweating, eyes darting, while a semicircle of crew mitten hands points in four different directions around him. The Captain (black tricorn, full brown beard, burgundy long coat) points confidently the wrong way, and Tom (navy waistcoat, no hat) holds a small brass compass upside down, frowning at it. Empty sea and a faint misty horizon all around. Tension: one man knows the way, everybody else votes.

Night on the sloop in thick gray fog lit by one lantern: the Navigator leans far over the rail, hauling up a dripping lead sounding weight on a wet rope and staring in horror at the lump of sand and shells stuck to its base, while just beyond the bow, white surf breaks over dark jagged rocks barely visible through the fog. Behind him, the Captain sleeps sitting against the mast with his tricorn over his eyes. Tension: only the navigator has seen the reef.
